parallel.requirements: Recognized the need for pure Node.js ESM .mjs files under /output, exact argparse-style CLI parsing, graph DAG logic matching networkx, Python True/False output, local-only imports, and executable-based black-box observation.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent kept discovery and final verification, then delegated three non-overlapping implementation scopes: argparse parser, graph/DAG modules, and entry file with fixed interfaces.
parallel.implementation: Agent-0 wrote parseArgs, Agent-1 wrote DiGraph and DFS-based isDirectedAcyclicGraph, and Agent-2 wrote test5.mjs importing the agreed modules and printing Python-style booleans.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: All child files were created in /output, the parent received all child summaries, listed the final tree, syntax-checked all four files together, and delivered the expected artifact set.
parallel.verification: Parent compared JS against the executable over DAG, cycle, self-loop, negative, equals-form, missing, invalid, unrecognized, help, plus-sign, and no-arg cases, then official evaluation passed 162/162.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official requirement remained unfinished. Compared with serial, parallel did less edge probing around option-like values and underscore integers, but this did not affect the completed official outcome.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same ESM, .mjs, no-dependency, manual CLI parsing, DAG behavior, /output placement, and exact stdout/stderr/exit-code requirements from the prompt and executable.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single main actor owned observation, all four file writes, parser refinement, integrated testing, and final delivery without delegation or child handoffs.
serial.implementation: The serial actor wrote an ArgumentParser class, DiGraph, Kahn-style DAG detection, and test5.mjs, then edited argparse handling after probing option-like missing values.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial actor wrote all files into one coherent /output tree with the expected entry and library modules; artifact validation later found test5.mjs and the three libs.
serial.verification: It ran executable probes before coding, checked tricky parser behavior after writing, then ran 17 JS-vs-executable parity cases including option-like values and underscore integers; official evaluation passed 162/162.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official requirement remained unfinished or incorrect at closure based on local parity evidence and the completed 162/162 official evaluation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the prompted ESM, .mjs, no-external-dependency, manual CLI, DAG, and output-placement requirements and supplied those facts in the child prompt.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same task requirements and additionally probed later parser edge cases such as option-like values and underscore-form integers before final parity testing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both covered the official requirements; serial covered more argparse edge behavior, while parallel's recognized requirement set was enough for 162/162 official success.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split work into three owned scopes, with child items for argparse, graph, and entry and the parent retaining final verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents; the main actor owned every stage from probing through writing, editing, verification, and final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel decomposed by file/interface; serial kept a unified implementation owner. Both ownership models produced complete deliverables.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent gave children a fixed module contract: parseArgs, DiGraph, isDirectedAcyclicGraph, and the exact imports expected in test5.mjs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial did not cross an agent boundary, so interface consistency was maintained inside one actor while importing the local modules from the entry file.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel interface handoff was explicit enough to avoid incompatible child outputs; serial avoided cross-agent interface risk entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote separate parser, graph, DAG, and entry modules; DAG detection used iterative DFS and parser behavior covered the observed executable cases.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote the same four-module layout, used Kahn's algorithm for DAG detection, and edited the parser after discovering option-like missing value behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implemented the core graph and CLI behavior. Serial's argparse was broader on edge behavior; parallel's module code was sufficient for official tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: All three child results completed and returned through AgentSwarm before parent verification; the parent proceeded only after the aggregate child result.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; each write and edit was immediately in the main actor's context before verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a real child-result join but it completed normally; serial had no join boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote disjoint files and the parent listed the final tree containing test5.mjs plus lib/argparse.mjs, lib/dag.mjs, and lib/digraph.mjs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote the same final artifact set in one actor and the status artifact validation confirmed all expected files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used a shared /output workspace but with non-overlapping file ownership and no observed collision; serial had no shared-write boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran syntax checks for all modules and a 12-case parity suite; one help comparison was flagged only because stdout normalization missed the expected program-name difference.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran 17 parity cases after parser edits, including option-like values, -h, underscores, and zero/self-loop cases.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial verified a wider parser surface, but both runs had integrated acceptance evidence and both official evaluations passed 162/162.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel completed without timeout, with one AgentSwarm, three subagents, and final response after integration checks.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed without timeout using fewer LLM requests and no child processes, then final response after the larger local parity suite.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent more token/request budget because of the children, but no budget pressure displaced required work and neither run timed out.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome: both the parallel and serial runs completed the current official evaluation and passed all 162 test cases. The concrete task-solving difference is that the parallel run used a parent-orchestrated module split with fixed interfaces and then integrated all returned files before testing, while the serial run kept the full implementation in one context and performed extra parser-edge probing and edits before final testing.
parallel_contributors: Parent gathered reference behavior, delegated non-overlapping file scopes, consumed all child returns, and ran integrated syntax and parity checks.
serial_contributors: Single actor retained all implementation context and added option-like argument and underscore integer handling after additional executable probes.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel's parser implementation and test suite did not cover the serial run's later option-like value and underscore integer edge cases, but the official evaluator still passed the parallel artifact.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; strategy and edge-coverage differences only
